Tablespoon(s) extra virgin olive oil
Tablespoon(s) ginger-minced

cinnamon stick
Clove(s) cloves
/2 Teaspoon(s) peppercorns-whole
Ounce(s) pearl onions Directions:
Preheat oven to 300 with rack in lowest position.

Cut beef into 1-inch pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper; toss with flour to coat. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches adding just enough oil to coat pot between batches. Transfer beef to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tablespoon oil, ginger, and garlic to pot; cook until beginning to soften, about 3 minutes.
Return beef to pot; add broth and prunes.
Wrap cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns in cheesecloth, tie with kitchen twine, and add to pot.
Bring to simmer.
Cover and cook in oven 2 hours.
Meanwhile, cook onions in boiling salt water until tender. About 15 minutes.
Once beef has cooked 2 hours, add onions to beef and bake 30 minutes more.
Break up prunes; remove spice bundle. Let cool completely; refrigerate up to 5 days.
Place potatoes in a saucepan, cover with 2 inches of water and add 2½ teaspoon salt.
Combine carrots and parsnips in another pan; cover with 2 inches of water, and add 1½ teaspoons salt.
Bring vegetables to a boil, reduce heat and simmer until fork-tender.
Drain vegetables.
Heat milk and butter until butter is melted.
Mash vegetables together; stir in milk mixture.
Season with salt and pepper. Let cool completely.
Refrigerate up to 5 days.
Preheat oven to 375. Spoon beef stew into baking dish(es). Cover with vegetable mash; sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 50 minutes.
Let cool 15 minutes before serving.

Shepherd's Pie
 
Save Print
Author: Genevieve Hammil
Ingredients
  • 4 Pound(s) beef chuck roast
  • 3 Tablespoon(s) all-purpose flour
  • 3 Tablespoon(s) extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 Tablespoon(s) ginger-minced
  • 4 Clove(s) minced garlic
  • 4 Cup(s) chicken broth
  • 1 Cup(s) pitted prunes
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 10 Clove(s) cloves
  • ½ Teaspoon(s) peppercorns-whole
  • 10 Ounce(s) pearl onions
  • Vegetable Mash ( Required ) :
  • 3 Pound(s) potatoes, cubed
  • 1 Pound(s) carrots-skin peeled and chopped into big 3 inch chunks
  • 1 Pound(s) parsnips-peeled, cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 1 Cup(s) whole milk
  • ½ Cup(s) butter
  • 1¼ Cup(s) grated cheddar cheese
Instructions
  1. Tablespoon(s) all-purpose flour
  2. Tablespoon(s) extra virgin olive oil
  3. Tablespoon(s) ginger-minced
  4. Clove(s) minced garlic
  5. Cup(s) chicken broth
  6. Cup(s) pitted prunes
  7. cinnamon stick
  8. Clove(s) cloves
  9. /2 Teaspoon(s) peppercorns-whole
  10. Ounce(s) pearl onions Directions:
  11. Preheat oven to 300 with rack in lowest position.
  12. Cut beef into 1-inch pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper; toss with flour to coat. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches adding just enough oil to coat pot between batches. Transfer beef to a plate.
  13. Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tablespoon oil, ginger, and garlic to pot; cook until beginning to soften, about 3 minutes.
  14. Return beef to pot; add broth and prunes.
  15. Wrap cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns in cheesecloth, tie with kitchen twine, and add to pot.
  16. Bring to simmer.
  17. Cover and cook in oven 2 hours.
  18. Meanwhile, cook onions in boiling salt water until tender. About 15 minutes.
  19. Once beef has cooked 2 hours, add onions to beef and bake 30 minutes more.
  20. Break up prunes; remove spice bundle. Let cool completely; refrigerate up to 5 days.
  21. Place potatoes in a saucepan, cover with 2 inches of water and add 2½ teaspoon salt.
  22. Combine carrots and parsnips in another pan; cover with 2 inches of water, and add 1½ teaspoons salt.
  23. Bring vegetables to a boil, reduce heat and simmer until fork-tender.
  24. Drain vegetables.
  25. Heat milk and butter until butter is melted.
  26. Mash vegetables together; stir in milk mixture.
  27. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool completely.
  28. Refrigerate up to 5 days.
  29. Preheat over to 375. Spoon beef stew into baking dish(es). Cover with vegetable mash; sprinkle cheese on top.
  30. Bake 50 minutes.
  31. Let cool 15 minutes before serving.
